title: Add contextual metadata checkpoints and release categories for changelog curation
author: Linnea Gomez
description:
Context and motivation: model onboarding churn makes release notes noisy. We need structured checkpoints that capture the state of onboarding metadata (performance profile anchors, provenance fingerprints, dataset tags) at key moments so the changelog synthesizer can generate concise, category-aware release notes. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) contextual metadata checkpoints — small, signed payloads recorded during onboard/accept flows, and (2) release categories — a lightweight taxonomy used by the changelog generator to group and prioritize changelog entries (e.g., perf, security, metadata, deprecation, backcompat).

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a new "checkpoint" object to the onboard transaction that serializes a concise snapshot of relevant metadata (profile hashes, sample coverage tags, quantization hints, affinity anchors).
- Persists checkpoints in the registry as compact records and emits them to the changelog-assembler service via the existing events bus.
- Introduces a release category field on generated changelog items and a mapping table that translates checkpoint deltas to category suggestions (configurable heuristics).
- Adds unit and integration tests for checkpoint roundtrip and changelog categorization heuristics.
- Adds an admin CLI command (ml-registry checkpoint:inspect) for debugging checkpoints and a small web console view to preview the suggested release categories for a model version.

Small illustrative snippet (checkpoint proto summary):
message Checkpoint {
  string id = 1;
  string model_id = 2;
  string version = 3;
  repeated string profile_hashes = 4;
  map<string, string> tags = 5;
  int64 created_at = 6;
  bytes signature = 7;
}

Why this approach: Compact checkpoints let us decouple changelog generation from raw telemetry while keeping provenance and profile context close to the model version. By mapping small, explainable deltas to categories we reduce noisy changelog entries (e.g., minor profile recalibrations) and highlight high-impact changes (e.g., new quantization profile or dataset license change).

Backward compatibility: checkpoints are additive — older registry clients ignore new records. The changelog consumer falls back to the previous heuristic if no checkpoint is present. Checkpoints are versioned in the proto so future fields are safe.

Operational notes:
- Checkpoints are compact and TTL'd at 90 days by default; we surface them in the console for 30 days.
- Signing keys live in KMS and are rotated quarterly; the onboard flow rejects unsigned checkpoints in strict mode (opt-in).
- We added a small rate-limit on checkpoint emission to avoid storms during large onboard batches.

QA and testing performed:
- Unit tests for proto serialization and DB compact-table reads/writes.
- Integration test exercising full onboard -> checkpoint persist -> changelog generation path.
- Manual e2e in dev cluster: onboarded two synthetic models (small/large), validated category suggestions in console and final changelog output.

Docs: short docs added at docs/registry/checkpoints.md explaining the checkpoint lifecycle, category mapping, and how to opt into strict signature verification.

Related work and references: ENG-4821 (release notes quality), ENG-4899 (onboard telemetry pruning), SUP-3142 (customer request for clearer changelogs).

Merge strategy: squash and merge.
